- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction.
- If model shows steady upward trend with no recent dip, true price often reverses or drops sharply; reduce forecast slope.
- After a sharp spike in price, model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak.
- When sentiment is neutral or negative (≤0.0), model often underestimates downside risk; add 1–3% buffer for downward correction.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion to prior 5–10 day average, model should adjust forecast toward that mean, especially if sentiment is weak.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture early volatility spikes; reduce forecast sensitivity to recent 3–5 day moves.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.2 spikes, model tends to overreact; apply smoothing filter to prevent overcorrection.
